source.title_on_document: Competition and Diversity in Generative AI

paper_design_summary: A game-theoretic model in which n producers sample content from a generative AI tool and earn less when others produce the same content type. The paper proves that stronger competition yields more diverse equilibrium output (Sections 3 to 5). It then simulates the game with six small open-source language models playing Scattergories, where each simulated player chooses a sampling temperature (and, in Section 6.2, a model). No human participants take part.

assignment.what_was_assigned: No people were assigned. Simulated players are LLM samples; each player's strategy is the sampling temperature (Section 6.1) or the pair (model, temperature) (Section 6.2).
assignment.quote: Our empirical setup is simple: n players each use an LLM to generate a single response to a Scattergories instance given by a (letter, category) pair.

participants.who: No human participants. Six LLMs (gemma2, llama3.1, llama3.2, mistral, nemotron, phi3.5) generate answers; qwen2.5 validates them. 25 (letter, category) instances; 2,000 samples per (model, temperature, instance).
participants.quote: Our experiments compare six LLMs, each of which is a relatively small open-source language model
participants.locator: p. 18, Section 6; p. 84, Table 1; p. 85, Table 2

ai_tool.name_model: gemma-2-2b-it, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, Nemotron-Mini-4B-Instruct, Phi-3.5-mini-instruct; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as answer validator
ai_tool.how_used: LLMs generate Scattergories answers at varying temperatures; no human uses them.

task.description: Scattergories: give a word or short phrase that starts with a given letter and fits a given category; a player scores only if the answer is valid and, depending on the score function, unique.

company_involvement.description: Single author at MIT Sloan and MIT EECS; no company role stated.

eligibility.reason: Theory paper with a model-only simulation: LLMs play Scattergories against each other. No people are assigned to AI, no people produce output, and no human output is compared with AI output. The codebook lists model-only and theory papers in the screening report only.

one_line_finding: In a game-theoretic model and in simulations where six small LLMs play Scattergories, equilibrium sampling temperature (output diversity) rises with the number of competing players, stays below the socially optimal temperature, and the model best in isolation (llama3.1, valid answer 92% of the time at n = 1) is overtaken by phi3.5 as competition grows (pp. 19-21, Figures 4 to 6).
notes: Proof appendices (Sections A and B) contain no empirical work. Section 6.3 validates Assumption 1 with 11 prompt variants and 3 temperatures per model (|Theta_I| = 33) on 10 of the 25 instances (pp. 22-24, 88-89). Only the arXiv v2 version was examined.
